attributes.step_input:
value='Final Cohort Definition

1) Index event
   - First condition occurrence of influenza during the 2-year study period. "Influenza" is defined as the OMOP standard concept 'Influenza' and all descendant concepts (all influenza subtypes and clinically-coded influenza diagnoses). The index date is the condition occurrence start date.

2) Entry criteria
   - Person has a condition occurrence matching the influenza concept set (see Index event) with event date within the study period (see Time window).
   - Person has continuous observation for at least 365 days immediately prior to the index date.
   - No requirement on sex; include all sexes.
   - Include all ages (age at index >= 0).

3) Population constraints
   - Limit to one index event per person: the earliest qualifying influenza condition occurrence within the study period that also meets the 365-day prior observation and the incident-case criterion (see Assumptions).
   - Persons must be observed in the database (have a continuous observation period) through the index date.

4) Visit / setting
   - Include influenza condition occurrences from any care setting (inpatient, emergency, outpatient, urgent care, telehealth) — do not restrict by visit type.

5) Time window
   - Study period = the 2-year period immediately prior to the analysis end date.
     - Analysis end date = the date the analysis is executed (ANALYSIS_DATE). Study start date = ANALYSIS_DATE minus 2 years.
     - Index events must occur between Study start date (inclusive) and Analysis end date (inclusive).

6) Exclusions
   - No clinical exclusions (user requested none).
   - Do not exclude vaccinated patients or any comorbidities unless a later revision is requested.

7) Exit
   - Cohort end date = index date (i.e., zero-day cohort duration). The cohort represents an occurrence event (index day only).
   - If needed for incidence-rate numerator calculations, this cohort is designed to represent incident influenza events; person-time for denominators should be derived separately from the at-risk population definition.

8) Assumptions
   - Assumption: By "rate" we interpret the user intends an incidence rate (cases per person-time) over the past 2 years. Therefore the cohort is defined to capture incident influenza cases.
   - Assumption: To ascertain incident cases, require no influenza diagnosis in the 365 days prior to the index date. That is, in addition to the 365-day continuous observation requirement, exclude persons with any influenza condition occurrence in the 365 days before the candidate index event. The retained index will be the first influenza occurrence within the study period that has no influenza in the prior 365 days.
   - Assumption: "Past 2 years" means the two full years immediately prior to the analysis execution date (ANALYSIS_DATE minus 2 years through ANALYSIS_DATE). If the implementer prefers fixed calendar dates instead (e.g., 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-31), substitute those explicit dates.
   - Assumption: Age grouping (user requested grouping by age) is not encoded into the cohort definition itself. The cohort includes all ages; age stratification will be applied during analysis. Recommended age strata (if implementer needs defaults): 0–4, 5–17, 18–49, 50–64, 65+ years.
   - Assumption: The influenza concept set includes all descendant concepts of the OMOP standard concept for Influenza and excludes non-diagnostic vaccine administration codes, lab result codes that do not represent a diagnostic condition, and influenza-like illness codes unless they map to the influenza concept descendants. Implementer should build and validate the concept set in ATLAS.

Notes for implementation in ATLAS
   - Create a concept set named "Influenza (standard concept + descendants)" including all appropriate diagnostic concepts and their descendants; explicitly exclude vaccine administration concepts.
   - Define cohort entry as the first condition occurrence within the study period; add the prior-observation and prior-influenza-exclusion logic as cohort inclusion criteria.
   - Use the cohort (incident influenza cases) as the numerator for incidence-rate calculations and define a separate denominator cohort (population at risk and person-time) for rate computation and age stratification.

If you want a prevalence-based rate instead of an incidence rate (for example, counting any person with influenza during the 2-year window regardless of prior history), or different age bins, or a different prior-observation requirement, tell me which alternative and I will update the cohort definition accordingly.'

WITH earliest_observation AS (
  SELECT
    person_id AS subject_id,
    observation_period_start_date AS cohort_start_date,
    observation_period_end_date AS cohort_end_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation_period`
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id ORDER BY observation_period_start_date ASC) = 1
)
SELECT
  1 AS cohort_definition_id,
  p.person_id AS subject_id,
  eo.cohort_start_date,
  eo.cohort_end_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` p
JOIN earliest_observation eo
  ON p.person_id = eo.subject_id
ORDER BY subject_id;
